found.why: The Chozeh of Lublin (from the Maggid of Rovno): 'ותרב חכמת שלמה' means Solomon took wisdom from everything; the wisdom of the children of the East and of Egypt helped his wisdom grow. Rav Tzadok's own reading of ותרב as 'grew by' what he drew out of them.

Solomon grew wise because he first learned the wisdom of the children of the East and so knew light's advantage over darkness; therefore his wisdom is 'chochmah tata'ah', a receiving wisdom. Same pairing of Solomon's lower wisdom with drawing from the East, and light out of darkness.

On the same parashah: 'ותרב חכמת שלמה מכל בני קדם' may mean that from the very wisdoms of the evil inclination true wisdom increased ('who is wise? one who learns from every man'). Same reading of the verse, applied to the yetzer rather than the nations' hidden Oral Torah.

Maharal raises Rav Tzadok's exact difficulty: Abraham cannot have given them sorcery, which the Torah punishes, so 'names of impurity' meant only demon-lore or remedies against sorcery. Rav Tzadok solves the same problem otherwise, with Paneach Raza's 'a Name in impurity'.

footnotes.text: **Zohar, Chayei Sara 26:264** (Kabbalah): opens with 'וַתֵּרֶב חָכְמַת שְׁלֹמֹה מֵחָכְמַת כָּל בְּנֵי קֶדֶם' and makes the children of the East the descendants of Abraham's concubines' sons, the sorcerers of the East. This is the passage Rav Tzadok quotes, and it ties together the verse, the sons of Keturah and sorcery. "אִלֵּין אִינוּן דְּהֲווּ מִבְּנֵי (אינון) בְּנֵי פִּילַגְשִׁים דְּאַבְרָהָם"

**Zohar, Chayei Sara 25** (Kabbalah): Keturah is Hagar, who strayed after her father's idols and afterwards bound herself to fit deeds, so her name was changed. It has both sides of Rav Tzadok's Keturah: deeds made fit, a root in Egypt. "קְטוּרָה דָא הִיא הָגָר... לְבָתַר אִתְקַּשְׁרָא בְּעוֹבָדִין דְכַשְׁרָן"

**Maharal, Gur Aryeh on Genesis 25:6** (Machshava): Maharal has the same difficulty: Abraham could not have handed them sorcery, which the Torah punishes with death, so the 'names of impurity' were only for driving sorcery and demons away. Rav Tzadok solves the same difficulty with Paneach Raza's 'a Name in impurity'. "אבל שיהיו משתמשים בכשפים – אין נראה לומר כלל, שהרי התורה חייבה מיתה מי שהוא מתעסק בכשפים"

**Avodat Yisrael (Maggid of Kozhnitz), Zevachim 62b** (Chassidus): he too reads R. Tarfon's 'Yochani' as a deliberate hint the nephews missed: 'יוכני', prepare me to open my mouth in Torah; and 'sons of Keturah' as קטורא, a bond, since he was bound above. The method is Rav Tzadok's, the meaning is different. "והם לא הרגישו בדבר ואמרו לו קטורה כתיב. אז קרי עליהם בני קטורה"

footnotes.ref: Divrei Emet, Divrei Emet on Torah, Balak 7
footnotes.text: **Divrei Emet (the Chozeh of Lublin), Balak 7** (Chassidus): citing the Maggid of Rovno, Solomon took wisdom from everything, and 'וַתֵּרֶב' tells what his wisdom grew from: the wisdom of the children of the East and of Egypt. This is Rav Tzadok's reading of וַתֵּרֶב as 'increased by' what he drew out of them. "וזה ותרב חכמת שלמה וקאמר ממה נתרבה מתכמת בני קדם בא לו עזר שנתרבה חכמתו וכן מחכמת מצרים"

**Maggid Devarav LeYaakov 93** (Chassidus): Solomon grew wise because he first learned the wisdom of the children of the East and saw light's advantage over darkness, so his wisdom is called the lower wisdom, which receives from something else. Rav Tzadok likewise calls Solomon's wisdom חָכְמָה תַּתָּאָה and has it grow from what it drew out of the East. "שנתחכם מחמת שלמד תחילה חכמת בני קדם והכיר יתרון אור החכמה עילאה מן החושך ולכך נקרא חכמת שלמה חכמה תתאה"

**Degel Machaneh Ephraim, Chayei Sara 6** (Chassidus): on the same parashah, he offers that true wisdom grew 'from all the wisdom of the children of the East', that is, out of the evil inclination's own wisdoms, as 'who is wise? one who learns from every man'. Rav Tzadok applies the same reading to the Oral Torah drawn out of the nations. "מכל חכמת בני קדם היינו מאותם החכמות עצמה של היצה\"ר נתרבה החכמת אמת"
